a.answer: Let R(x)=(x^2-4)/(x-2). Its domain is R\{2}, since x-2=0 exactly at x=2. For x≠2, x^2-4=(x-2)(x+2), so R(x)=x+2 by cancellation of the nonzero factor x-2. Thus the simplified expression is x+2, conditional on x≠2. It agrees with the original at every input in the original domain, but they are not equivalent as functions on all real numbers: x+2 is defined at x=2 and equals 4 there, whereas R is undefined there.
